Hisano et al. (1104.0228) find the leading-order electroweak-loop SI cross section of pure EW-multiplet DM (including the higgsino, n=2, Y=1/2, evaluated at M=1 TeV) to be O(1e-46 to 1e-48) cm^2, suppressed by an accidental cancellation: twist-2 contributions are positive while Higgs-exchange, gluon and scalar contributions are negative, and they are of similar size. The cross section is nearly independent of mass above about 1 TeV.
LZ 2024 (2410.17036, 4.2 tonne-years): the strongest SI exclusion is 2.2e-48 cm^2 (90% CL) and the best median sensitivity is 5.1e-48 cm^2, both at 40 GeV/c^2. The abstract quotes no value at 1 TeV.

Correction to f-008: an upper bound below 1e-48 cm^2 compared with the LZ minimum of 2.2e-48 cm^2 (at 40 GeV) is a factor of more than 2.2 (more than 0.34 decades), not 2 orders of magnitude. The comparison that actually matters is at the same mass. At 1.1 TeV the linearly rescaled LZ limit of about 6e-47 cm^2, divided by the bound of 1e-48 cm^2, gives a ratio of at least about 60 (at least about 1.8 decades). That ratio is still an estimate: the LZ and XENONnT curves at 1 TeV were not read.
